[[17592186551286 :question/worked-solution "We write down $N$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply an elementary row operation that transforms the left matrix into the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{}[N\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{array}{cc|cc}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{12} & 0 & 1\end{array}] &  & {R}_{2}:=12{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{array}{cc|cc}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 12\end{array}]\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse is obtained on the right-hand side of our big matrix after the transformation. Therefore, 

$$
{N}^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 12\end{bmatrix}.
$$"]]
